newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese prosecutor blocks journalist's release.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese prosecutor blocks journalist's release.

text.p: A Lebanese military judge ordered the release on Friday of a journalist charged with contacts with Israel but the chief military prosecutor immediately appealed against the decision, judicial sources said.

The journalist, Maronite Christian Pierre Atallah of the conservative daily an-Nahar, was still held at the military tribunal in Beirut awaiting a decision by a military court of appeal which was not expected before Monday, the sources said.
They said prosecutor Nasri Lahoud lodged the appeal after Judge Riad Taliya ordered Atallah's release on a surety of one million Lebanese pounds ($647).

Atallah, 34, is the last of some 48 people rounded up last month after a van carrying Syrian workers was machinegunned in a predominantly Christian area north of Beirut, killing the driver and wounded some passengers.

All the other detainees have been released. Only one, Ghassan Bardaweel, was charged like Atallah with "disturbing Lebanon's relations with a friendly country" -- a reference to Syria whose 35,000 troops in Lebanon make it the country's main power broker.
Atallah was also charged on December 30 with "making contacts with Israeli enemy agents and distributing leaflets that incite soldiers against obeying orders".

The Paris-based press freedom watchdog group Reporters sans Frontieres (Reporters Without Borders) has appealed to Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and French President Jacques Chirac for Atallah's release.

Gibran Tueini, one of the owners of an-Nahar, said last month Atallah was seized during the night by a Lebanese Army officer and an army intelligence agent who refused to show an arrest warrant but put guns to his head and took him to an unknown place.
An-Nahar's lawyer later found that he had been taken to the defence ministry outside Beirut.
